newsitem.title: USA: CBOT-CME talks on common initiatives to continue.
newsitem.headline: CBOT-CME talks on common initiatives to continue.

text.p: Talks between the Chicago Board of Trade and Chicago Mercantile Exchange on common banking and processing will continue in January, regardless of the results of a cost-benefit survey sponsored by the exchanges' Joint Strategic Initatives Committee, several exchange and clearing house officials said.
"The common initiatives will continue regardless of how that study proceeds and what the findings in it are," said John Hiatt, president of the Board of Trading Clearing Corp.
Hiatt and other representatives of the joint initiatives committee were speaking on a panel at the Futures Industry Association's annual conference here.

The CBOT, the CME and the Clearing Corp, which is the CBOT's independent clearing house, jointly hired the outside consultant Electronic Data Systems Corp to identify costs in three phases of consolidation.
The first phase of the EDS study is on common data processing, followed by studies on common software applications and the benefits of common clearing.
"The urgency level (for common processing) in 1996 is greater than in 1990 or 1993," said Larry Mollner, FIA head and executive vice president of Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.

"We will see the results of the EDS study at the first of the year," Mollner said. "It will be up to the leadership of the committee to continue the work." -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
